question: Does the original host-redistribution-associated resource assemblage homogenization exceed a newly matched fixed-margin null after adding all accepted-ID-resolved BCE/Clarke rank1-3 host link candidates to the fixed host list of the exact European subset?

source.BCE_Clarke: BCE-derived Clarke 2024 evidence 1-3, 83 species-level evidence-bearing pages within 92 exact-butterfly matches, not original Dryad data

analysis.comparability_primary: Keep EXACT 355 WGSRPD3 regions that had ANY native resource opportunity in ORIGINAL 239 butterfly-region matrix. Comparative Jaccard and fixed-margin null tests use same fixed domain for original and BCE-augmented panels.
analysis.secondary: Report native-active domain after augmentation and new region count separately, descriptive only; never compare secondary domain to 355-region null.
scenarios: original host inventory, original native and contemporary
all 1027 BCE-identified unique accepted host edges added to same butterfly as evidenced; no changes to remaining species
analysis.null_method: Use original analyze_butterfly_resource_homogenization.py swap_null preserving each butterfly added region count, each region added opportunity count and native incidences as forbidden, separately for each scenario
outcomes: fixed-margin null median, 95% interval and Monte Carlo one-sided p
acceptance: Hard fail if reconstructed original species metrics or exact 355-region observed Jaccard differ from frozen reference beyond 1e-9
Hard fail on nonmonotonic native/contemporary footprint or null margin breach
No favorable host subset tuning if evidence fails

claim_boundaries: This is Europe-derived literature-host-source upper-bound extrapolation, not corrected global ecological truth
No observed butterfly colonization, survival, competition, abundance or host quality inferred
No original GEB manuscript or PR38 changes
